title: DoubleAdapt: A Meta-learning Approach to Incremental Learning for Stock Trend Forecasting

problem.claim: Stock trend forecasting must update continuously as new stock data arrive, but future data distributions may differ from incremental data and hinder effective model updates.

gap.claim: Incremental learning for stock trend forecasting remains under-explored because of distribution shifts, also called concept drifts.

contributions.claim: DoubleAdapt is an end-to-end incremental-learning framework with separate data and model adapters for mitigating distribution shifts.
The framework automatically adapts stock data toward a locally stationary distribution and adapts model parameters under mitigated distribution shifts.
Each incremental-learning task is formulated as a meta-learning task to optimize data adaptation and parameter initialization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world stock datasets are reported to show state-of-the-art predictive performance for DoubleAdapt.
Experiments on real-world stock datasets are reported to show considerable efficiency for DoubleAdapt.

narrative_sequence.summary: Stock trend forecasting is important for quantitative investment, and stock data arrive continuously in online settings.
Incremental updates can incorporate recent patterns, but changing data distributions make effective updates difficult.
DoubleAdapt addresses distribution shifts through data and model adapters, including adaptation toward local stationarity.
The framework casts incremental-learning tasks as meta-learning tasks to optimize adaptation and parameter initialization.
Experiments on real-world stock datasets are reported to demonstrate predictive performance and efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates adaptation of incoming data from adaptation of model parameters under distribution shifts.

interpretation.claim: Incremental learning may benefit from treating input-distribution correction and parameter updating as coordinated but distinct responsibilities.

application.claim: For online forecasting systems, consider separate mechanisms for making new data more locally stable and for initializing or updating model parameters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation generalizes beyond stock forecasting or which distribution shifts it handles best.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the real-world stock datasets, prediction targets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the adapter architectures, meta-learning procedure, update schedule, or computational efficiency measurements.
